about.unesco_desc_start: Shining with its historical and cultural richness, Edirne is under worldwide protection with the masterwork of the genius architect Mimar Sinan,
about.unesco_desc_end: , and the centuries-old Kırkpınar Oil Wrestling.
about.ottoman_desc: Serving as the capital of the empire before the conquest of Istanbul, Edirne is practically a living open-air museum with its palaces, stone bridges, inns, and mosques built during this period.
about.location_desc_start: Edirne, Turkey's border gate to Europe, is a neighbor to Greece and Bulgaria. Given life by the
about.location_desc_end: rivers, this city has been a transit point of cultures for centuries.

storiesScreen.headerSubtitle: Edirne legends passed down through generations

stories.title: The Legend of the Inverted Tulip
stories.spot: A symbol of stubbornness and sorrow in the Selimiye Mosque...
stories.content:
There is an inverted tulip motif in the stone carvings of the muezzin's gathering place in the Selimiye Mosque.

According to the rumor, there was a tulip garden belonging to a woman in the area where the mosque was to be built. The woman did not want to give up her garden and delayed the start of the construction. Eventually, a part of the garden was taken, but this event was not forgotten. Mimar Sinan carved the tulip upside down to symbolize this stubbornness and the trouble experienced.

According to another interpretation, the inverted tulip represents sorrow, mortality, and humility before God.

stories.title: The Healing House of the Health Museum
stories.spot: Healing that comes to souls with the sound of water, music, and beautiful scents...
stories.content:
Built by Sultan Bayezid II in 1488, the hospital was one of the most advanced health centers of its time.

Here, instead of being chained, mental patients were treated with:
• The sound of water,
• Bird sounds,
• Music therapy,
• Beautiful scents.

According to a story told among the people, some patients experiencing severe mental problems would calm down by listening to the sound of flowing water and reed flute performances for days, and would even be discharged completely healed. For this reason, the building was known as the 'palace that distributes healing'.

stories.title: The Wait on the Meriç Bridge
stories.spot: A sad love legend extending from the war years to the present day...
stories.content:
There is a romantic story told among the people about the Meriç Bridge.

During the war years, a young soldier promises to return to the girl he loves. The girl comes to the bridge every day and waits for him. However, the soldier cannot return. It is said that the tears of the young girl waiting on the bridge for years mixed with the Meriç River.

For this reason, some elderly residents of Edirne say that the river flows sadly when they look at the bridge at sunset.

stories.title: The Legend of the Three-Balcony Minaret
stories.spot: Three mysterious paths climbing up without ever seeing each other...
stories.content:
The Üç Şerefeli Mosque gets its name from its minarets with different numbers of balconies.

According to the rumor, the architect of the mosque challenged the masters of the period by designing each of the minarets differently. In particular, the fact that the three separate stairs going up to the minaret with three balconies reach the top without seeing each other is described as a 'master's secret' among the people.

stories.title: The Birth of Kırkpınar
stories.spot: The legendary heroes of forty springs gushing out in the lands of Rumelia...
stories.content: The origin of the Kırkpınar Oil Wrestling dates back to the years of transition to the Rumelia sanjak of the Ottoman Empire. It harbors the legendary story of forty brave wrestlers who could not defeat each other in matches that lasted for hours among the raiders. The forty springs that gushed out where they wrestled symbolize the sacred lands where this tradition was born today.
